notes: SHIP v1.14.390 - TWO DEVICE DEFECTS, FIXED SEPARATELY. DEFECT 1, RACK VISUALIZATION DID NOT LOAD. The decisive fact: the canvas mounted every time in a desktop harness and failed on device, so this was a LIFECYCLE defect, not a missing call, a wrong host or a CSS collapse. bw_render() runs the instant showPage(work) fires, so #bw-mount can still measure ZERO while the page is mid-transition; rackElevation_render3D then builds a 0x0 canvas, throws nothing, and leaves a blank area - exactly the reported symptom. THE CORRECTION IS LIFECYCLE, NOT SCENE: the mount now waits for a host with real clientWidth and clientHeight before drawing, bounded to ~40 frames (about 0.7s, longer than any transition in this app), then calls the SAME existing renderer. Nothing in the scene was touched - lighting, materials, fog, tone mapping, tray geometry, TYPE_COLORS, floor, reflection and rack hardware are all untouched, and the renderer still owns its own GL lifecycle and single-context guard. THE FAILURE NOW PROVES ITSELF ON THE DEVICE. There is no console in a cold aisle and a blank box is the one thing a tech cannot report, so every failure path writes console.warn AND phantomToast AND prints a one-line diagnostic INSIDE the card carrying rack id, host in-DOM, width, height, clientWidth, clientHeight, window.THREE, real WebGL availability and whether a dispose hook exists. Six distinct stop points are now named rather than silent: renderer absent, rack null, loadScript absent, three.js fetch failed, three.js loaded but window.THREE missing, host never measured, renderer returned without a canvas, and renderer threw. If it fails again the card states which one. The flat no-WebGL path is preserved. DEFECT 2, BUILD UI VISUAL QUALITY. The workspace read as separate legacy blocks in a container because each block carried its own margins, radii and type sizes. There is now ONE spacing system declared on #bw-shell - outer padding 15, section gap 15, card padding 17, control gap 9, radius 20, secondary control 46, primary action 56 - and every direct child is separated by that single gap, so no block needs a margin of its own. The one-off local margins are deleted. Hierarchy now reads in the required order: BUILD / FIELD MODE, honest on-device status, Active Rack hero, phase and progress, CONTINUE, Next Action, rack preview, controls, metrics, contextual actions, bottom nav. The rack ID is 38px and CONTINUE is 56px, so both dominate the first screenful. ONE CONTROL LANGUAGE: FRONT, ISO, TOP, REAR, CABLES and EXPLODE are the renderer OWN pills, restyled to 46px with a 12px radius and one type scale - and scoped to .bw-prev ONLY, so the rack-detail panel copies keep the look they already ship with. OPEN AISLE matches that height and stays visually distinct as the door out. Verified uniform: all camera segments report a single distinct height. Controls sit ABOVE the render area and never overlap it; the mount is a stable 268px. Metrics are a deliberate 2x2 on phone with 22px values instead of microscopic type. Contextual actions share one height, radius and padding. Sentence copy lost its shouty tracking; only technical labels keep it. VERIFIED AT 393: canvas mounts, no diagnostic shown, CTA 56, camera pills 46 and uniform, OPEN AISLE 46, actions 54, metrics two columns, mount 268, zero horizontal overflow. NOT DONE AND NOT CLAIMED: this is a harness pass in Chrome. The device pass is yours, and defect 1 in particular can only be confirmed on the iPhone that showed it. If the rack still fails there, the card will now tell you exactly where it stopped - send me that line.
